correctness.rationale: For step order L>=4, the +a and -a frequency characters in each squared STFT slice are distinct. Equality of measurements therefore recovers s_x=|f_x|^2+|f_{x+a}|^2 and c_x=f_x conjugate(f_{x+a}). Full support makes c_x nonzero. Quotients q_x of two solutions satisfy q_x conjugate(q_{x+a})=1, forcing constant phase and alternating moduli r,r^{-1} on each step cycle. The sum equation factors as (r^2-1)(r^2|f_x|^2-|f_{x+a}|^2)=0, giving exactly the trivial cycle phase or an alternating two-level magnitude pattern. The converse swap preserves both recovered coefficients. The finite verifier uses exact rational/Gaussian-rational arithmetic and is corroborative, not the proof of the infinite statement.

originality.rationale: The archive-era sufficient conditions do not settle the equal two-point even-order window because its zero-shift ambiguity has a half-cycle zero. The prior almost-all theorem allows but does not classify exceptional full-support signals. Later exact work on windows with ambiguity zeros focuses its complete short-window results on separated signal classes and records the almost-all nonvanishing result, not the exact alternating-magnitude fiber. published-finding corpus and own-ledger comparisons found no implication covering this statement.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently phrased derivation of the equal two-point exceptional full-support fiber may exist.

value.rationale: The theorem gives the exact exceptional set behind an existing almost-all uniqueness result for the simplest degenerate short window, precisely in the parity regime where standard ambiguity-nonvanishing criteria fail. It supplies the entire phaseless fiber and a sharp global-retrievability criterion, explaining the obstruction by an even-cycle bipartite level swap. This is a structural boundary theorem with direct relevance to uniqueness, not a routine parameter extension or finite recomputation.
